results.title: User preferences a fresh editor mounts with
results.about: 4.13.0: the accelerator asks for snapping, and `isSnapMode` turns that around. The default decides which way a plain drag behaves.

known.reason: mocanvas keeps the raw preferences sparse on purpose — an unset key means 'whatever the editor's default is', and `UserPreferencesManager`'s getters resolve it — so `getUserPreferences().animationSpeed` is undefined where tldraw's is 1. An app that multiplies a duration by it gets NaN. Decide: resolve in the getter, or keep the distinction and say so in COMPAT.md.
Same sparse-preferences design: undefined rather than false. Falsy either way, so behaviour matches; a `=== false` check does not. See the animationSpeed entry, which is the one that actually breaks.
Same sparse-preferences design as isSnapMode.

results.title: An auto-sized text shape, per font and size
results.about: End to end: the font stack the library ships, its line height and its measurement, in the two numbers a consumer's layout actually reads.

known.reason: Label widths, because the two libraries are not setting the same type. mocanvas ships no font files and borrows local families (Helvetica, Georgia, Comic Sans MS, Menlo); tldraw ships its own. Measured 2026-11-12 on 'Hamburgefonstiv': mono within 0.3%, sans -3.1% to -7.5%, serif -7.9% to -8.2%, draw -8.8% to -9.1%. Decided 2026-11-12 to carry the difference rather than vendor four typeface families: the package not carrying fonts is worth more than the last few per cent of width, and an app that needs the exact widths replaces the theme's font stacks. Written up in docs/COMPAT.md. Line height is NOT part of this — 4.17.0 aligned it exactly.

`zoomToFit`, by default and at stated insets
results.about: Split in two on purpose: with the inset stated, this is the fit arithmetic; with it left out, it is only the default, and a difference in one is a different bug from a difference in the other.

known.reason: `zoomToFit()` with no inset leaves twice the margin here. The arithmetic is identical — at a stated inset of 0, 64, 128 or 256 both land on the same camera to five decimals — so the whole difference is the default: mocanvas uses min(256, viewportWidth * 0.28), which is 256 in a 1200x800 viewport, against tldraw's 128. A migrated app that calls zoomToFit sees its content smaller.
